questions.explanation: Fronting the object 'this' focuses it; no inversion is needed with a fronted object.
Fronted 'out' with the verb of motion inverts dramatically: 'Out ran the children'.
Fronted predicative adjectives invert with 'be': 'Gone are the days'.
questions.q: ___ are the days of cheap oil.

questions.explanation: 'However' + adjective + subject + verb inverts the usual order for formal concession.
Fronted negative adverbials trigger inversion: 'On no account must'.
'Here' + 'come' agrees with the plural subject: 'Here come the guests'.
Fronted 'such' + 'be' inverts for rhetorical emphasis.
questions.q: ___ was the noise that we had to leave.

questions.explanation: Fronting the prepositional object focuses the recipient; the order stays otherwise normal.
Fronted 'never before' triggers inversion for dramatic emphasis.
Fronted negative 'not a word' inverts the auxiliary and subject.
Fronted 'only then' triggers inversion in the clause it introduces.
questions.q: ___ did I understand the scale of the disaster.

questions.explanation: Fronted 'so' + adjective inverts with 'be' for emphatic result.
questions.q: ___ was she that she fell asleep at the table.

questions.explanation: 'There' fronted with 'stood' presents the scene with literary focus.
questions.q: ___ stood the old castle on the hill.

questions.explanation: Fronting the demonstrative object focuses it emphatically without inversion.
A fronted adverbial of place can invert with the verb for dramatic focus.
Fronting the direct object puts contrastive stress on 'the money'.
questions.q: Which sentence correctly fronts the object?

questions.explanation: Fronted predicative 'happy' with 'be' inverts for exclamatory focus.
Fronted locative phrases with verbs of position invert the subject and verb.
options: On the hill the church stood.
On the hill stood the church.
On the hill did stand the church.
Stood on the hill the church.

questions.explanation: 'Here' + 'comes' agrees with the singular subject in presentative fronting.
Fronting the infinitive phrase focuses the action denied.
